hypotheses.paper: M_0 globally hyperbolic singular flat spacetime
hypotheses.note: an abstract Geometry (Level A) with s₀ : 𝔊.Str M₀, T2, connected, GH; the singular flat case is the Level-B instance (packages 11, 12, gx)

hypotheses.paper: globally hyperbolic (no Cauchy surface assumed; ETT.tex:1885, these.tex:6288)
hypotheses.note: cbg and its corollaries also assume a Cauchy surface S: the library's GloballyHyperbolic (Causal/Properties.lean:144) is causal + compact diamonds and gives none, and without one no Dev exists; recoverable at the singular flat instance via theo:geroch_sing (ETT.tex:1771, DEC-18), never for an abstract Geometry
DEC-59: universal (Sbierski Thm 2.8); the ETT form is the corollary cbg_isETTMaximal, and isETTMaximal_iff_isUniversal shows the two readings agree once cbg holds

sorries.obstruction: SORRY(theo:CBG): the target of the campaign, proved in CBG/Maximal (design §3 steps 1–7)

findings: ETT §4's printed setting (abstract morphisms IsEMorphismOn, ETT.tex:1849–1852) has no universal development: in causalPreGeometry the timelike half-line has no universal development (not_exists_isUniversal_halfLineDev, via kinkIso), and the candidate ℝ is not ETT-maximal (not_isETTMaximal_halfLineDev: arctanSelf is a non-surjective Cauchy self-embedding fixing ]-∞,0], isCauchyEmbedding_arctanSelf). Non-existence of an ETT-maximal development (and failure of uniqueness) in the ETT reading is NOT proved. DEC-60's ruling, in this proved extent

rem:CBG_analytique (ETT.tex:1903–1910) quotes rigidity for morphisms 'defined on a connected manifold'; it also needs a Hausdorff TARGET: any morphism predicate containing the two inclusions ℝ → branching line (ETT.tex:1312) is not rigid (not_isRigidFor_branchingLine)

rem:CBG_manquant (i) (ETT.tex:2343–2356): in the thesis framework a (G,X)-variété is second countable by definition (these.tex:1357–1359), so the limit's second countability is an obligation; here it is a geometry field (A2, SingularFlatAxioms.secondCountable for every Hausdorff connected admissible structure) — proved for regular flat (DEC-49), open with singular charts (R2)

The Cauchy-surface hypothesis of cbg is a ⚠ strengthening of theo:CBG / theo:Cauchy_ext ('globally hyperbolic' only); recoverable at the singular flat instance via theo:geroch_sing (DEC-18), not for an abstract Geometry

Design §2's T2 witness proper (without T2 carriers the branching line IS a minimal over-extension, so CommonSubExtension/CommonOverExtension must ask T2) is not formalized; only rigidity failure into a non-T2 target is (not_isRigidFor_branchingLine)

Audit fix (blocking): the former single field LocalModel.localUnique had an unconstrained regular branch; with regularChart, the groupoid inverse and sing_mem it forced an element of G sending all of 𝕄 into reg(𝔼_α), impossible by the developing map, so gx's model 𝕄 ⊕ Σ_α 𝔼_α could not instantiate Level B. Split into localUnique_sing (thesis def:analytique, these.tex:3335–3340: f : reg(U) → reg(Y) with MapsTo into the connected component of the singular point y₀, i.e. the same model) and localUnique_reg (this file's own Liouville branch, with MapsTo into fully regular components). The flat instance is unaffected
questions: these.tex:3176 defines X_A-morphisms by a condition 'pour tout x ∈ sing(M)' only; read as every x ∈ M (regular points: charts in X, these.tex:3043; consistent with the equivalence of these.tex:3398–3407)

these.tex:3177–3182 asks one g ∈ G_Y on EVERY connected open W of the chart overlap; Level B uses the local form LiftPropOn G.IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt, which agrees on injective maps by B1 + B2 (localUnique). Is the strong form needed anywhere gx relies on?

A3 (germExt_future/past) extends ψ at EVERY corresponding boundary point (Sbierski Lemma 3.8, Def 3.5 = MapClusterPt q (𝓝[U] p) ψ); the thesis extends only under J(Σ,p)∖{p} ⊂ N (prop:Cauchy_non_max, these.tex:6634–6640). gx: is A3 true at BTZ points without that hypothesis (it should be, via K⁻(p)∩J⁺(Σ) ⊂ U from lem:corresponding_K, these.tex:6558)? If not, A3 must carry the (3.10)-type hypothesis and package 6 must route Lemma 3.9 accordingly

B2's same-model hypothesis (localUnique_sing MapsTo into connectedComponent y₀) replaces famille analytique (b) / def:incompatibles (these.tex:3328–3332, 3346–3353). gx: confirm that at a BTZ corresponding boundary point the transported ψ lands in the component of the chart image of p (package 11 derives it from sing_mem + the chart at q)

Geometry and LocalModel have no inhabitant in this file (kb/0011, kb/0012). Before the gate closes: check the flat LocalModel field by field (Y = Minkowski d, singY = ∅, G = isometry groupoid, regularChart := refl, localUnique_sing vacuous, localUnique_reg = Liouville)

hypotheses.paper: two E≥0-morphisms on a connected manifold agreeing on a non-empty open set agree
